case_name: Shane Roy Needham v. Janet Lea Needham

issues.label: Standard of review on appeal
issues.why: The court must determine the appropriate standard for reviewing the magistrate court through the district court's intermediate appellate decision.

issues.label: Abuse of discretion in property division
issues.why: The central question is whether the magistrate court abused its discretion in dividing the community Alturas shares.

issues.label: Proper valuation date for shares
issues.why: The court must decide whether the shares should have been valued as of the divorce decree date, trial date, or another date.

issues.label: Failure to value the shares at all
issues.why: The magistrate court declined to assign any value to the shares, raising whether valuation was legally required.

issues.label: Equal versus unequal division
issues.why: The court must assess whether the in-kind division actually achieved the substantially equal division both parties requested.

issues.label: Application of Idaho Code 32-712 factors
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the statutory community property division factors were properly considered and applied.

issues.label: In-kind division of closely held stock
issues.why: The court must decide whether dividing shares of a closely held corporation in-kind is appropriate under Idaho precedent.

issues.label: Distinguishing Josephson and Lamm
issues.why: The court must determine whether those precedents preclude or permit dividing closely held corporate stock here.

issues.label: Effect of division on minority shareholder value
issues.why: Whether creating two minority stakes impairs the marketability and value of the shares must be assessed.

issues.label: Authority to compel BSA Waiver execution
issues.why: The court must decide whether the magistrate court had power to order Mr. Needham to sign the waiver.

issues.label: Whether Waiver alters the BSA
issues.why: The court must determine if the BSA Waiver improperly amends or circumvents the parties' Buy-Sell Agreement.

issues.label: Enforceability of BSA against community property
issues.why: Whether the BSA's book-value repurchase and transfer restrictions bind the court's division of community shares.

issues.label: Ms. Needham's consent to BSA
issues.why: Her signed acknowledgment agreeing to be bound may affect how the community interest can be transferred.

issues.label: Effect of missing shareholder consent
issues.why: The BSA Waiver required all three shareholders' assent, and Mr. Needham's refusal raises validity of the transfer.

issues.label: Third-party rights of non-party shareholders
issues.why: Pearson and Woods' contractual rights under the BSA may be affected by the ordered transfer.

issues.label: Court disentanglement of the parties
issues.why: The court must weigh whether the ordered division leaves the ex-spouses improperly entangled through joint ownership.

issues.label: Consideration of deadlock rationale
issues.why: Whether breaking corporate deadlock is a proper basis for a divorce court's property division must be examined.

issues.label: Treatment of natural enhancement in value
issues.why: The court must address whether post-decree appreciation should benefit both parties and how to allocate it.

issues.label: Availability of monetary award alternative
issues.why: Whether the magistrate court should have fashioned a buyout with installment payments as Mr. Needham requested.

issues.label: Impact on Mr. Needham's board seat
issues.why: The court must consider whether stripping voting control and board position was an equitable consequence.

issues.label: Frivolous appeal attorney fee award
issues.why: The propriety of the district court's fee award for a frivolous appeal must be reviewed.

issues.label: Attorney fees on current appeal
issues.why: The court must decide whether either party is entitled to fees for the present appeal.

issues.label: Reserved jurisdiction over shares
issues.why: The validity and scope of the magistrate court's reservation of jurisdiction over the shares may bear on its authority.

issues.label: Treatment of interim dividends
issues.why: The court must consider how the post-decree dividends already split affect the overall equitable division.
